page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.large is an arm64 compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the AWS Graviton family featuring ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores. The configuration provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core, accompanied by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 4.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, does not include local disk storage, and operates without GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent single-core capabilities contrasted with low overall throughput due to the small core count. In single-threaded execution, the instance posts a Geekbench single-core score of 1783.0 and achieves strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.24 GB/sec. Stress-ng single-core performance registers at 1707.29, within the median range. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks show typical lower-tier scaling, with a multi-core stress-ng result of 3400.48, Geekbench multi-core score of 3208.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 1982.47. In-memory and caching operations achieve 4.63 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.87 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, c8gn.large delivers dedicated ARM-based compute cycles and 6 Gbps network capability without the overhead of larger multi-socket configurations. However, the lack of integrated local storage necessitates network-attached storage via EBS, and the 4.0 GB memory ceiling restricts memory-intensive applications. The instance is suited for lightweight network-bound services, single-threaded processing tasks, proxy nodes, microservices, and general compute-optimized utility workloads that do not demand extensive parallelism.

It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per core. Operating without integrated local storage or GPU hardware, the instance relies on network-attached storage and features a 6 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark testing reveals solid single-threaded performance, including 14.24 GB/sec in single-core bzip3 decompression and a Geekbench single-core score of 1783.0. Multi-core and bandwidth limits reflect the small two-core profile, recording 3400.48 in stress-ng multi-core and 4.63 million Redis SET operations per second. The server offers an efficient resource footprint tailored for lightweight network proxies, microservices, background job workers, and single-threaded compute tasks.
